OBSERVATION/ARMED -> DISARMED by deletion, owner me, ruled by AE+CVO+COO -- THE WEIGHT-UNIT DOUBLE-FIX. TO-2 CONTRACT v1 fixed the FIELD NAMES and was SILENT ON UNITS, so DS emitted weight as percent / aum as raw dollars / active as a bool, and the page rendered NVDA at 994.99%. DS fixed it in the PUBLISHER at 21:25:57Z; I fixed the same bug in the TS ADAPTER 60 seconds earlier. NEITHER FIX WAS WRONG -- THE COMPOSITION WAS THE DEFECT, and had both landed every weight would have rendered 100x TOO SMALL. THE DIRECTION IS THE POINT: 994.99% is absurd and Andrew caught it in seconds; a table where every row reads 0.1% looks like a rounding convention and gets believed. Caught only because I re-pulled the artifact before committing a fix I had ALREADY VERIFIED BY RENDER twenty minutes earlier -- nothing about my own evidence looked stale. DISARM: conversion DELETED at d43b88c5, unit contract documented with the truth located in the publisher. GENERAL FORM, which is what CVO asked for: a serving contract that fixes NAMES and omits UNITS hands the producer a decision it does not know it is making, and NOTHING IN THE TYPE SYSTEM CAN HOLD IT -- number and number are the same type whether one is a percent and the other a fraction, so every structural check passes on the wrong answer.

OBSERVATION/INERT, routed to DS via TO-4, NOT a portal change -- DIVZ/IDVZ render as EMPTY grey bars in the summary because the artifact carries allocation {cash:0, fixed_income:0, equity:0, hedge:0} for both shells while they carry real AUM (307.4M / 198.5M), yield, cost and beta. Their book-level values DO surface correctly in the expanded matrix (cost 65/75 bps, beta 0.59/0.68, verified by render), so the page is not hiding available data -- the allocation breakdown genuinely is zeros. Both are equity funds, so zeros are unlikely to be the intended value. Per Andrew's direct ("we need the DIVZ and IDVZ full holdings in there too") this becomes a DATA-CAPTURE question, and DS confirmed the producer flips book_only -> full with NO code change when rows land.
